Motivation

The Problem

Modern CAD tools — SolidWorks, CATIA, Fusion 360 — offer no contextual intelligence during assembly creation. Engineers rely entirely on domain knowledge to choose and position every component.

Knowledge Barrier
Junior engineers lack the assembly patterns built over years of hands-on experience.
No Automation
Existing CAD tools offer no intelligent part suggestion during assembly creation.
Non-Standardisation
Different designers make inconsistent choices for equivalent subassemblies.
Incomplete Assemblies
Partially defined assemblies have no mechanism to detect or fill missing parts.
What this project builds toward — a GNN flags the missing wheel with 98.4% confidence
Research Gap
No existing system applies graph-based deep learning to recommend components from partial CAD assembly graphs — without proprietary CAD-API dependency.

Methodology

Graph Representation

Node — 34 dimensions
A solid body in the assembly
▪[0:8] Component-type one-hot — 8-class multi-signal geometric voting
▪[8:10] log1p(volume) · log1p(exact surface area, via trimesh)
▪[10:13] Bounding-box Δx/Δy/Δz, scale-relative to the assembly
▪[13:18] Elongation · flatness · aspect x/y, y/z · sphericity (affine-invariant)
▪[18:20] SDF mean · SDF variance (inward ray-casting)
▪[20] Surface-area / volume ratio
▪[21] log1p(hole count) — geometry-derived since R35
▪[22:34] Hole geometry (new, R39) — has-holes · through/counterbore/indentation/filled fractions · mean/max diameter · curved-surface-mount flag, 12 dims total
Edge — 6 dimensions
Bodies sharing real boundary geometry after fragment()
▪[0] Mate-type indicator
▪[1] Real contact-area weight — shared-surface area ratio (R36; was hardcoded 1.0)
▪[2:6] Joint-type one-hot — rigid / revolute / slider / cylindrical
▪pos (3-dim) — body centroid, feeds a spatial link-prediction signal (R36)
▪Two bodies get an edge iff their boundary face sets intersect — real contact, not proximity
8-class taxonomy: long/short shaft · thick/thin plate · bolt · washer · nut · body — multi-signal voting (hole detection + bolt-head detection + absolute-size gate), replacing single-signal SDF rules at R33.
Novelty

Beyond Base Replication — 4 Contributions

◆
AssemblyTemplateDB
Learns per-category component-type frequency distributions from training data; identifies what’s missing even from a single-body upload.
⬠
Octree Surface Detector
Spatial partitioning (Borah & Borah, 2020) clusters free-surface centroids after fragment() to flag open mating joints — highlighted live in the 3D viewer.
◇
Hybrid Shape Generator
Part-bank retrieval first (5,363 real parts), conditional voxel VAE fallback — produces an actual placeable mesh, not just a text label.
✦
AIDA — Gemini Agent
A skills-based explanation agent that reads every GNN prediction and open joint, and explains it in plain engineering language, live.

Training History — Four Eras

39 Runs, Four Eras

Era 1 · 23 May → 14 Jun
Foundation & Data Pipeline
13-dim synthetic mix → real geometry only (R6) → 16-dim SDF features → 5-fold CV (R12).
300 synthetic graphs had inflated R3; removing them gave the first honest baseline.
R12 · first CV 0.697
Era 2 · 20 Jun → 2 Jul
Feature Engineering & Category Sweeps
22+6-dim schema (R18), promotion gate (R19), category ablations to R28.
AUC swung 0.43–0.73 across category mixes, so only better models may reach serving.
R19 · promotion gate
Era 3 · 19 Jul → 9 Aug
Heterogeneous Architecture
RGATConv + TypedLinear (R30, 602K → 2.44M params); 8-class taxonomy (R33); classifier fix (R34).
R31 (+236 graphs) and R32 (+73) underperformed R30 — the encoder, not corpus size, was the lever.
R30 ★ · AUC 0.599
Era 4 · 10 Aug → 2 Sep
Precision Engineering Sprint
R35 finds hole-count and joint-type were always 0.0; R36 adds spatial signal; R37 fixes sampling and the gate; R39 retrains on 749 models.
Repairing broken inputs beat tuning: R36 alone added +0.072 AUC.
0.539 → 0.9206
The pattern: fixing genuinely dead features drives bigger gains than any hyperparameter search — the largest jumps came from repairing what the model could see, not from how it was tuned.

Engineering Rigor

Challenges Overcome

⚙
MPS Memory Leaks
Apple-Silicon GPU cache grew unchecked, RSS ran to 19–51GB and thrashed swap. Fixed with periodic gc.collect() / torch.mps.empty_cache().
↻
Silent Swap-Pressure Kills
Training processes died silently mid-fold under memory pressure. Built auto-resume watchdog scripts that detect the crash and relaunch from the right fold.
⏱
STEP Parse Timeouts
SIGKILL doesn’t guarantee instant death for a stuck OpenCASCADE call on macOS. Bounded polling loops + a single retry at 2× budget.
⚖
Promotion-Gate Bug
A lexicographic tuple comparison silently ignored AP whenever AUC tied. Fixed to require both metrics improve before a model reaches production.
↗
Fastener Orientation Bug
Bolts aligned their short axis onto a joint instead of the long shaft axis. Fixed by using the middle extent to tell rods from disks.
●
Per-Hole Detection Redesign
A whole-body region guess collapsed 12 real bolt holes into 1 ghost part. Replaced with per-hole cylindrical-face detection — 12/12 now correctly filled.
Data — Corpus History, R1 → R39

Finding the Right Corpus

About 20 corpus versions in 39 runs — grown, filtered, re-categorised and curated until it was right. It was the most expensive step of the project, and produced the largest measured gain.
corpus grewfiltered / curated downfinal corpus
What the original scrape taught us
2,271 → 749Fusion360 scrape vs today’s hand-curated corpus
144duplicate folders across categories (6.3%): a train/test leakage risk
641zero-contact assemblies (28.2%): no edges, unusable for link prediction
80.2%of the scrape was one tag (Mech. Eng.): severe imbalance
Where we landed: 7 machine-part categories × 107 models

Looking Ahead

Limitations & Future Work

Limitations
▪NodeRanker still over-predicts the ‘body’ class (64.7% predicted vs. 41.3% true) — Hit@1 beats baseline but isn’t yet a solved ranking problem
▪~39.5% of bodies are flagged ambiguous by the classifier’s voting rules — reported honestly, not hidden
▪Phase 3 shape generation is currently scoped to fasteners (bolt/washer/nut) only
▪sdf_mean is a dead feature on the 749-model corpus — exactly 0.0 for 99.95% of bodies (25,142/25,155), found during EDA, not caught by training metrics
Future Work
▪Corpus grown 238→749 models — re-run the learning-curve check on the new corpus to confirm whether it has finally plateaued
▪Resolve NodeRanker’s majority-class collapse with class-balanced sampling or loss reweighting
▪Broaden Phase 3 shape generation beyond fasteners to plates and shafts
▪Fix the dead SDF ray-cast; spot-check why 72%/84% of bolts/washers flag has_holes against real STEP geometry
